answer: Agents trading willow, dune and delta surveys get voting passes at simultaneous in-person check-ins. Registrars admit each person once, mark entrants and sign one pass bound to an agent key and epoch. Validators check the signature and reject reused pass serials; a forged pass earns no vote. One body cannot attend two venues at once, so each extra identity requires recruiting another person. Running more software in parallel creates no passes. Security assumes honest registrars, physical presence checks and a check-in window shorter than travel between venues.
